svg.title: RIEMANN-MASULLO-DIAGRAMS DD — Appendix D · AppD_SchwartzBruhat, declaration by declaration
svg.desc: riemann-masullo at 72a10ff: the 1,634 declarations of the 144 items on CD, each with its kind, file, line and state; 98 declarations with a Deviation: line, quoted.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Posters: M1, what the targets rest on · M2, the steps with no known repair · M3, the paper by depth · M4, every chapter · M5, the refutations. Names, items, files, entries and posters are links, underlined under the pointer: a card's title or a Lean name opens the source at the pin.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: How to read it. The expansion of CD's cards, in the same order: one block per item, its heading opening the card. First the declarations whose docstring states how the Lean departs from the print, each with its Deviation: line quoted from the Lean source (Apache-2.0), then every declaration of the item. A name opens its line at the

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: pin. A declaration's state is read from the terms: open when it uses sorryAx, resting when something open is below it. That a declaration states what its Deviation: line says is the docstring's claim, not checked here.

g.text: This proof assumes a second-countable group and an available Plancherel measure. The Fourier isometries on two distinct cosets would give a nonzero integrable density on their disjoint union with every character integral equal to zero.

g.text: The page states the equivalence for measurability with respect to the quotient measure and the Haar measure of the group. This is the form for Borel measurability, which is what the printed proof establishes; the form for the two completed measures is not stated here.

g.text: This isolates the local exponential map. After equipping the group with a compatible Lie group structure, its exponential is a homomorphism by commutativity and is a local homeomorphism by the inverse function theorem and translation.

g.text: This isolates the local chart construction. On a sufficiently small compact identity neighborhood the homomorphism is an embedding. In logarithm coordinates its image near zero is a relatively closed local additive subgroup of a finite-dimensional real vector space, hence locally a linear subspace. Translation gives charts at every point.

g.text: This is the projector identity described after (D.1.6.26), with the forward transform on both paths and both compact averages taken with mass one. The ill-typed inverse-transform formula (D.1.6.25) is left open.

g.text: The first proof paragraph on p. 776 prints $k'k/k'$ as the compact subgroup in the pair for $G/k$. We use the image $k'k/k$ of $k'$.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The displayed map on p. 776 averages over $k'k/k'$. The kernel on the source stage $\Gamma'/k'$ is the image $(k\cap\Gamma')k'/k'$.

'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: This is the case of one stage of the inductive limit; the general case follows by additivity.
